title: Limits of the level-independent fall: level superpositions, records, the operator under the factor

key_results.statement: Exact in the gradients and in $\kappa$, for every $\alpha$, $g$, $\chi$, $\lambda$: $p_x=\sum_k\lvert\alpha_k\rvert^2p^{(k)}_x$ and $\bar x_{\rm lab}=\sum_k\lvert\alpha_k\rvert^2\bar x_k$; it rests on the conservation of the level and the orthonormality of the $\lvert f_k\rangle$.

Drift acceleration of $\Phi_\sigma[\alpha,g]$ (first order, long chain, long window at fixed $g$, then sharp label): $\sum_k\lvert\alpha_k\rvert^2a_{k,\sigma}(p_0)$; the same for all $\alpha$ iff $a_{k,\sigma}(p_0)$ is level-independent, at rest line 1 or 2 of (4.19), no new condition.

Starts at rest, fixed smooth $g$, first order: $D=\tfrac14\lambda^4\operatorname{Var}_\alpha(\langle a_{\cdot,\sigma}\rangle_g)+E$ with $\lvert E\rvert\le r\lambda^3\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}_\alpha}+r^2\lambda^2$; in the sharp-label limit the coefficient of $\lambda^4$ tends to $\tfrac14\operatorname{Var}_\alpha(a_{\cdot,\sigma}(0))$.

Class $\mathcal C$, $\lvert\alpha_k\rvert^2=1/N$, sharp-label limit of the $\lambda^4$ part of $D$: zero for (a), (c); $\tfrac14\lambda^4\tau^4g^2m^2\mathcal V_N$ for (b1), (b2); $\tfrac14\lambda^4\tau^4g^2c_{\rm f}^2\mathcal V_N$ for (f).

Zero gradients, sharp-label limit: $v_k\to\sigma\omega_k'(p_0)=\sigma\tau_k^2\sin p_0\cos p_0/\sqrt{M_k^2+\tau_k^2\sin^2p_0}$; two levels have equal sharp-label velocities at $\sin2p_0\neq0$ iff $\tau_k^4/(M_k^2+\tau_k^2\sin^2p_0)$ is equal, which needs $\tau_k\neq\tau_{k'}$ for different data; a start of finite width can have equal velocities in all levels.
Bound, zero gradients, every start concentrated at $p_0$: $\lvert v_k-\sigma\omega_k'(p_0)\rvert\le\tfrac12\sup_p\lvert\omega_k'''\rvert\delta p^2$; $v_k\neq v_{k'}$ whenever $\delta p<\delta p_*$.
Exact in the gradients: $\mathrm d\bar p_k/\mathrm d\lambda=-\int\frac{\mathrm dp}{2\pi}c^\dagger B_kc+(c^\dagger B_kc)(p_0+\pi)$, with the weight crossing the cut of the arc.

First order, every smooth $g$, no window: $\mathrm d\bar p_k/\mathrm d\lambda=\langle\pi_{k,\sigma}\rangle_g-\lvert g(p_0+\pi)\rvert^2\pi_{k,\sigma}(p_0+\pi)$ with $\pi_{k,\sigma}(p)=\mathcal F_k-\sigma(G_kM_k+g_{\zeta,k}\tau_k^2\sin^2p)/\omega_k(p)$.

Bound, every start at rest: the first-order rate differs from $(1-\lvert g(\pi)\rvert^2)(\mathcal F_k-\sigma G_k)$ by at most $\tfrac12\sup_p\lvert\pi_{k,\sigma}''\rvert\delta p^2$; for sequences with $c_{\rm cut}\neq1$ the limiting rate is level-independent iff $\mathcal F_k-\sigma G_k$ is, and together with a level-independent drift acceleration $a\neq0$ iff also $\tau_k^2/M_k$ is, which is impossible in $\mathcal C$.

$P(a;\lambda)=\frac1N\sum_{k,k'}\alpha_{k'}^{*}\alpha_k\Gamma_{kk'}(\lambda)e^{2\pi i(k-k')a/N}$, exact with the medium in the level components; at leading order in $\kappa$ with the $\Gamma_{kk'}$ of the effective body contract.

Zero gradients, exact, every smooth $g$: $\Gamma^{(0)}_{kk'}=e^{-i(V_k-V_{k'})\lambda}\langle\cos\tfrac{\theta_k-\theta_{k'}}2e^{-i\sigma(\omega_k-\omega_{k'})\lambda}\rangle_g$; for even $g$, $\Gamma_{kk'}$ is exactly even in the gradients.

Exact, every smooth $g$, $p_0$, $\lambda$: $\Gamma_{kk'}[g;\text{gradients}]=\Gamma_{kk'}[g^-;-\text{gradients}]$ with $g^-(p)=g(-p)$; for starts of definite parity $\lvert\Gamma_{kk'}\rvert$ is exactly even in the gradients.

Exact Taylor expansion in the gradients at fixed $\lambda$ and start, where $\Gamma^{(0)}_{kk'}\neq0$: $\lvert\Gamma_{kk'}\rvert/\lvert\Gamma^{(0)}_{kk'}\rvert=1+\operatorname{Re}\epsilon_1+Q_2+O(\text{grad}^3)$, $Q_2=-\tfrac12\mathcal V+\tfrac12(\operatorname{Im}\epsilon_1)^2+\operatorname{Re}\epsilon_2$, with the bound $\lvert\epsilon_1\rvert\le\eta_0\mathcal V^{1/2}$.

Order of the first deviation of $\lvert\Gamma_{kk'}\rvert$, complete and exact: none for equal blocks (O0); degree one at a zero of $\Gamma^{(0)}_{kk'}$ (OZ); first order iff $\operatorname{Re}\epsilon_1\neq0$ (O1); second order iff $\operatorname{Re}\epsilon_1=0\neq Q_2$ (O2); otherwise third or higher (O3).

Exact, every smooth complex $g$, $p_0$, $\lambda\ge0$: the complete first-order term $\Gamma^{(1)}_{kk'}$, branch part plus inter-branch part, and $(\lvert\Gamma_{kk'}\rvert/\lvert\Gamma^{(0)}_{kk'}\rvert)_1=\operatorname{Re}(\Gamma^{(1)}_{kk'}/\Gamma^{(0)}_{kk'})$ where $\Gamma^{(0)}_{kk'}\neq0$.
Exact inter-branch amplitude $a_{k,\perp}$ of first order, with the bound $\lVert a_{k,\perp}\rVert\le A_{k,\perp}(\lambda)$.

Exact inter-branch part $\Gamma^{(1),\perp}_{kk'}$ with the bound $\lvert\Gamma^{(1),\perp}_{kk'}\rvert\le\tfrac12(\tau_k/M_k+\tau_{k'}/M_{k'})\langle\sin^2p\rangle_g^{1/2}(A_{k,\perp}+A_{k',\perp})$.

Bound, every start at rest: $1-\lvert\Gamma^{(0)}_{kk'}(\lambda)\rvert\le\epsilon_0(\lambda)=[\tfrac12\lambda\sup_p\lvert\omega_k''-\omega_{k'}''\rvert+\tfrac18(\tau_k/M_k+\tau_{k'}/M_{k'})^2]\delta p^2$, so $\Gamma^{(0)}_{kk'}\neq0$ where $\epsilon_0<1$.
Bound, every start at rest: $\delta x_g^2\delta p^2\ge C_g^2+\tfrac14(1-\lvert g(\pi)\rvert^2)^2$, hence $2\delta pX_g\ge\lvert1-\lvert g(\pi)\rvert^2\rvert$.

Class (N), range (N2), order estimate with exact coefficients in the local form: $Q_2\simeq-\tfrac12\operatorname{Var}_g(K_{kk'})=-[\tfrac12\lambda^2(\pi_k-\pi_{k'})^2\delta x_g^2+\tfrac12\sigma\lambda^3(\pi_k-\pi_{k'})\varpi_{kk'}C_g+\tfrac18\lambda^4\varpi_{kk'}^2\delta p^2]$, different from zero iff $(\pi_k-\pi_{k'},\varpi_{kk'})\neq(0,0)$ (exact lower bound).

Real Gaussian starts at rest, class (N), range (N2): $1-\lvert\Gamma_{kk'}\rvert/\lvert\Gamma^{(0)}_{kk'}\rvert\simeq\tfrac12\delta x^2(\pi_k-\pi_{k'})^2\lambda^2+\frac{\lambda^4}{32\delta x^2}(\nu_{k'}\pi_k-\nu_k\pi_{k'})^2$ with $\pi_k=\mathcal F_k-\sigma G_k$.

First order jointly in $G_k$, $\mathcal F_k$, $g_{\zeta,k}$ and $\kappa(\xi-\langle X\rangle)$, every smooth $g$ and every $\chi$: the first-order velocity is unchanged, and so are (4.7), (4.16), (4.19).

Zero gradients, exact pointwise in $p$: the coefficient $v_2(p,\lambda)$ of $\varepsilon^2$ in the velocity, with the secular term $\tfrac12\sigma\lambda^2\omega'''$ and three oscillating terms at the rate $2\omega$.

Zero gradients, Taylor expansion in $\kappa$ at fixed $\lambda$, start, chain: $v=\sigma\langle\omega_k'\rangle_g+\kappa^2\sigma_X^2[\tfrac12\lambda^2\sigma\langle\omega_k'''\rangle_g+R_2]+\kappa^3\mu_3[-\tfrac16\lambda^3\sigma\langle\omega_k''''\rangle_g+R_3]+O(\kappa^4)$; $R_2$ has a bound linear in $\lambda$, and $R_3=O(t_k\nu_k\lambda^3\mathcal D_k^{-1/2})$ is an order estimate for $\mathcal D_k\gg1$.
Exact, every smooth $g$ and $\lambda\ge0$: the change of the acceleration at order $\kappa^2$ is $\kappa^2\sigma_X^2\langle\partial_\lambda v_2\rangle_g$, with $\partial_\lambda v_2$ in closed form.

The orders of limits for the record terms, stated separately for the orders $\kappa^2$ and $\kappa^3$: case A (window average at fixed $g$, then sharp label in the coefficient), case A′ (instantaneous value for $\lambda\to\infty$ at fixed $g$, no window), case B (sharp label at fixed $\lambda$ or fixed window), and every smooth $g$ at every $\lambda$.

Exact, every smooth $g$ and $\lambda\ge0$: $a_2[g](\lambda)=\sigma\lambda\langle\omega_k'''\rangle_g+a_2^{\rm osc}[g](\lambda)$ with the bound $\lvert a_2^{\rm osc}\rvert\le\nu_kX_g\lambda+c_3[g]$, and $a_2[g]/\lambda\to\sigma\langle\omega_k'''\rangle_g$ for $\lambda\to\infty$ at every fixed smooth $g$.

Order $\kappa^2$, sharp-label coefficient of the secular part, obtained as a window average at $\bar\lambda$ (case A, under a sufficient window condition) and as the limit of $a_2[g]/\lambda$ (case A′): $\delta a^{(2)}_{k,\sigma}=-\kappa^2\sigma_X^2\lambda v(4+3\omega_k''(p_0)/\omega_k(p_0))$, near rest $-\kappa^2\sigma_X^2\lambda(4+3\tau_k^2/M_k^2)v$; zero at rest, level-independent near rest iff $\tau_k/M_k$ is.

Order $\kappa^3$ at rest, sharp-label coefficient of the secular part: $\delta a^{(3)}_{k,\sigma}=\tfrac\sigma2\kappa^3\mu_3\lambda^2\frac{\tau_k^2}{M_k}(4+3\tau_k^2/M_k^2)$; it is the leading part of the window average at $\bar\lambda$ under (7.48) and $\Lambda\ll\bar\lambda$ (case A), and it is not the instantaneous acceleration after dephasing (case A′, (7.50)).

Window averages at fixed smooth $g$: the bound $\lvert\overline{a_2}-2s_2\bar\lambda\rvert\le(2c_1[g]\bar\lambda+2c_0)/\Lambda$ and the identity $\overline{a_3}=3s_3(\bar\lambda^2+\Lambda^2/12)+(R_3(\lambda_1+\Lambda)-R_3(\lambda_1))/\Lambda$.

Order estimates, narrow start at rest with $\mathcal D_k\gg1$: $R_3\simeq\frac{\sigma t_k\nu_k^{1/2}w_0}{48\sqrt\pi}\lambda^{5/2}\cos(2M_k\lambda+\tfrac\pi4)$, and the rest of the window average of order $\kappa^3$ has the relative size $\varrho_{3,\rm win}\lesssim\frac{\sqrt2w_0}{3(4+3t_k)}\frac{1}{M_k\Lambda}\sqrt{\nu_k\bar\lambda/\pi}$.

Order $\kappa^2$, case A′, order estimates: $a_2^{\rm osc}$ is $O(\nu_kX_g\lambda\mathcal D_I^{-n})$ for every $n$ if the label weight is free of stationary points, and $\tfrac\sigma4\sqrt{\nu_k\lambda/\pi}\,\rho_s'\cos(2M_k\lambda+\tfrac\pi4)$, growing as $\lambda^{1/2}$, if it contains the stationary point $0$ or $\pi$.

Order $\kappa^3$ at rest, case A′, order estimate for a narrow start with $\mathcal D_k\gg1$ and $w_0\neq0$: $a_3[g]=3s_3\lambda^2+a_3^{\rm osc}$ with $a_3^{\rm osc}\simeq-\frac{\sigma\tau_k^3w_0}{24\sqrt\pi M_k^{3/2}}\lambda^{5/2}\sin(2M_k\lambda+\tfrac\pi4)$; $a_3[g]/\lambda^2$ has no limit for $\lambda\to\infty$, so without a window the acceleration is not (7.16).

Case B, order $\kappa^2$, near rest: $\kappa^2\sigma_X^2v[-(4+3t_k)\lambda+\lambda\cos2\omega\lambda+\nu_k\lambda^2\sin2\omega\lambda+\frac{2+3t_k}{2M_k}\sin2\omega\lambda]$, zero at rest; with an exact bound for the window average at a sharp label.

Case B, order $\kappa^3$ at rest, exact: $v_3(0,\lambda)$ and $\partial_\lambda v_3(0,\lambda)$ in closed form; the acceleration has the secular part $\tfrac\sigma2\nu_k(4+3t_k)\lambda^2$ and an oscillating part up to $\tfrac13\tau_k^2t_k\lambda^3$ at the rate $2M_k$; level-independent iff $(\tau_k,M_k)$ are.

Bound: $\lVert\mathrm d\bar x/\mathrm d\lambda\rVert\le c_k=\tau_kd_0$ for every state in the level $k$; it coincides with the bound (5.11) of 04-ilang-time/05-moving-clock iff the $\tau_k$ are equal.

Case A, near rest, background form of the secular record terms at $\bar\lambda$: $[-\lambda(4d_0^2+3c_k^2/M_k^2)u+\tfrac{\sigma\gamma_X}2\lambda^2\frac{c_k^2}{M_k}(4d_0^2+3c_k^2/M_k^2)]\hat e$, against the drift term $d_0a_{k,\sigma}(0)=\frac{c_k^2}{d_0M_k}(\sigma\mathcal F_k-G_k)$.
The secular record terms are smaller than the drift acceleration at rest where $\varrho_2<1$ and $\varrho_3<1$, that is $\lambda<\lambda_2$ and $\lambda<\lambda_3$.

Rests of the window averages relative to the drift acceleration: $\varrho_{2,\rm rest}$ (bound) and $\varrho_{3,\rm rest}=O(\kappa^3\lvert\mu_3\rvert t_k\bar\lambda^3/(\Lambda\mathcal D_k^{1/2}\lvert\sigma\mathcal F_k-G_k\rvert))$ (order estimate).

Sufficient, not necessary, at the retained orders: if $\varrho_2+\varrho_{2,\rm rest}+\tfrac43\varrho_3+\varrho_{3,\rm rest}\le\delta_{\rm acc}$ for every level involved, the window-averaged falls of two levels with the same drift acceleration agree to the relative accuracy $2\delta_{\rm acc}$.

Necessary and sufficient by definition, window averages at the retained orders, two levels with the same first-order window average $\bar a$: relative accuracy $\delta$ iff $\lvert\kappa^2\sigma_X^2(\overline{a_2}^{(k)}-\overline{a_2}^{(k')})+\kappa^3\mu_3(\overline{a_3}^{(k)}-\overline{a_3}^{(k')})\rvert\le\delta\lvert\bar a\rvert$; leading form in the regime (R): $\kappa^2\bar\lambda\lvert\tfrac12\kappa\mu_3\bar\lambda-\sigma_X^2p_0\rvert\lvert n_k-n_{k'}\rvert\le\delta\lvert\bar a\rvert$ with $n_k=\nu_k(4+3t_k)$.
$a_{k,\pm}(0)=-g\tau_k^2\pm\frac{\tau_k^2}{M_k}(\mathcal F_U-gu_k)$.

Fall from rest level-independent: upper branch iff $\tau_k^2[(\mathcal F_U-gu_k)/M_k-g]=a_+$ for all $k$; lower branch iff $\tau_k^2[-(\mathcal F_U-gu_k)/M_k-g]=a_-$ for all $k$; both with one value $a$ iff $gu_k=\mathcal F_U$ and $g\tau_k^2=-a$ for all $k$.

$C_{\rm eff}\mapsto C_{\rm eff}+c\mathbb 1$ acts as $(u_k,\mathcal F_U)\mapsto(u_k+c,\mathcal F_U+gc)$; well defined are $g$, $M_k$, $u_k-u_{k'}$ and $\mathcal F_U-gu_k$; not well defined are $u_k$, the statement that all $u_k$ vanish, and the statement that $u_k$ is proportional to $M_k$.

open_issues: The third order in the gradients of |Γ_kk'| (case (O3) of (7.36)) is outside the scope and not derived.
(7.32) and the remainder of (7.25) are order estimates with their calculations; no constants and no bounds are derived for them, apart from (7.29), (7.30), (7.31), (7.37).

R_3 in (7.14), its leading term and the relative rest of the window average in (7.48), and the oscillating parts (7.49), (7.50) are order estimates (leading stationary-phase terms, with their calculation); no bounds are derived for them, and none for the λ-derivative of R_3. For p_0 ≠ 0 in case B only the term of v_3 with the highest power of λ is given.
The instantaneous acceleration of order κ^3 of a fixed g away from rest (case A′, p_0 ≠ 0) is not determined; (7.50) is for starts at rest.
The second form of (7.51) is a leading-order statement in the regime (R). Outside (R) only the first form is available, and no necessary condition in single-level quantities is derived.
Terms that mix κ with the gradients, the order κ^4 and the second order in the gradients of the acceleration are outside the scope; (7.46) is a statement at the retained orders.
(7.3): the constant r of the bound on E depends on g; nothing is stated on D at fixed λ in the sharp-label limit.
The effect of an operator under the factor on the relation (4.24) outside the class C needs the clock rate of that body, which is not among the quoted inputs.

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions: (7.15), (7.16) and each term of (7.43) times κ^3 μ_3 have the dimension λ^-2 of (4.16); the terms of (7.38), (7.40) and the ratios of (7.18), (7.34) are dimensionless.

One level, a sharp X, a plain gradient only, a real Gaussian start: (7.1), (7.2), (7.8) reduce to the single-level start; no record term for a sharp X; (7.29) and Step 7 agree for a plain gradient; (7.38) reduces to (7.10), and (7.25) follows both from (7.24) and from the local form.

Short-λ expansions: (7.13) against the double commutator and (7.42) as its derivative; the coefficients of λ and λ^3 of (7.43) vanish; (7.47) in the sharp-label limit near rest gives −λv as (7.42) does; the pointwise coefficient behind (7.50) is the λ^3 sin term of (7.43), and the λ-derivative of the leading term of (7.48) is the leading term of (7.50); dimensions of (7.49), (7.50).
